thread.title: House committee advances Rep. Pfluger's bill on rural broadband deployment
thread.title_full: House committee advances Rep. Pfluger's bill on rural broadband deployment

author: Midland Times
title: House committee advances Rep. Pfluger's bill on rural broadband deployment
text:
The House Energy and Commerce Committee has unanimously advanced a bipartisan bill led by Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) aimed at improving transparency and efficiency in the broadband deployment process. The legislation, known as the Federal Broadband Deployment Tracking Act, seeks to address challenges faced by rural communities in accessing reliable internet services.
If enacted, the bill would require the National Telecommunications and Information Administration (NTIA) to submit a detailed plan to Congress within 180 days. This plan must outline how the agency will track permit applications for deploying broadband infrastructure on federal lands. The goal is to streamline projects that expand broadband access and help close the digital divide affecting rural areas.
During remarks delivered at the committee markup, Rep. Pfluger stated: "I rise in support of my bipartisan bill, H.R. 1343, the Federal Broadband Deployment Tracking Act, which I am leading with Congressman Soto."
He continued: "I’m proud that this is the first of many bipartisan bills to be considered in today’s markup, and I hope this committee can come together to deliver bipartisan solutions on energy efficiency and broadband permitting that deliver real results for the American people."
Rep. Pfluger explained that his bill aims to improve transparency and efficiency by streamlining processes related to Form 299, which is used for requesting access to rights-of-way or sites for broadband facilities on federal lands or buildings.
"At the recent broadband permitting hearing, we heard several examples that underscored the need for this legislation. Several broadband infrastructure providers detailed instances in which they had crews ready, equipment purchased, and federal funds allocated, but were left waiting for permits for an extraordinary amount of time," he said.
He also noted: "Last Congress, the House of Representatives unanimously passed the Federal Broadband Deployment Tracking Act. Passing the Federal Broadband Deployment Tracking Act would be a crucial step toward fixing this process and closing the digital divide, creating a more connected future for all Americans."
Rep. Pfluger concluded his remarks by urging support from both parties: "I urge my Republican and Democrat colleagues to support this legislation. Americans cannot afford to be left behind any longer."
August Pfluger has represented Texas’ 11th district in Congress since 2021 after succeeding Mike Conaway. He won his seat in 2020 with nearly 80% of the vote against Jon Mark Hogg.
